subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a native folder-backed encrypted snapshot flow with new `backup` config keys, or keep core to local archive/export while off-machine backup remains ClawHub/plugin-owned?
rationale: This PR adds new configuration, encryption-key handling, and destructive restore behavior in core; that is a product/security boundary decision beyond routine bug repair.

options.title: Sponsor native core snapshots after blockers
options.body: Keep the PR open, require the rebase/security/proof work, and let maintainers own the new core backup config surface.

options.title: Route off-machine backup to ClawHub/plugins
options.body: Keep core focused on local archive/export and ask contributors to publish folder/cloud snapshot tooling outside core unless a missing core API is identified.

options.title: Narrow to restore/export hardening only
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that preserves current backup create/verify behavior and defers setup/run/list encrypted snapshots to a separate product decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor native core snapshots after blockers
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, require the rebase/security/proof work, and let maintainers own the new core backup config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and hardened the existing backup CLI surface, so they are the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether this new core surface fits.
